To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) polar prototype networks are a class of neural networks that explicitly state the structure of the output space, 2) polar prototypes are a priori separated on the output hypersphere, 3) polar prototypes are used to define a polar distance between examples and classes, 4) training is performed by minimizing the angular distances between examples to their class prototype, and 5) the polar distance can also be used for regression, by interpolating between two prototypes.

polar prototype networks can be trained for classification and regression without learning the output space, and that the structure of the output space can be designed to achieve large margins and semantic priors.

polar prototype networks can perform classification and regression in an output space of arbitrary dimensionality, with the ability to learn a disentangled representation, and without the need to train layout structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how we can learn a neural network with a simple structure, while still being competitive in terms of accuracy.
the question of whether a simple structure can be effective for learning.
the design of networks with a structure that is explicitly defined in the output space, while maintaining the benefits of learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polar prototypes are a simple and powerful way of defining output structures, and that polar prototype networks can be applied to both classification and regression, with a single model.
polar prototype networks are a simple and effective way to perform classification and regression in an interpretable way, without the need for parametric learning.
polar prototype networks provide a new perspective on the problem of learning inductive structures, and that they are competitive to standard methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polar prototype networks provide an effective alternative for learning in the output space, which is both interpretable and competitive to standard methods.

polar prototype networks provide a simple and effective way to perform classification and regression without learning the layout of the output space, and that this is achieved by leveraging the geometry of the hypersphere and the simplicity of polar interpolation.
we are able to learn a simple structure in the output space, which can be exploited by a neural network to perform regression and/or classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the output space is an important factor in learning, which can be explicitly stated in neural networks.
the output structure is a fundamental part of the task at hand, which should not be learned from data.
we can learn the structure of the output space without learning a parametric function for the structure.
